title: T1090.003 — Proxy - Multi-hop Proxy
subtitle: A fictional but realistic company network.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: The rented first hop
steps.caption: The attacker rents a cheap VPS from a cloud provider. They install a port-redirector tool on it. The server becomes hop 1. Nothing about it looks special.
steps.defender: nothing on your network yet. The rental is invisible to you.

steps.title: The compromised second hop
steps.caption: The attacker scans for an old router at a branch office and gets in. They install custom firmware code on the router. The router becomes hop 2 and joins an ORB relay network.
steps.defender: still nothing. The router vendor never tells you.

steps.title: The implant lands
steps.caption: A phishing email reaches a finance workstation. The user opens the attachment and the implant installs. Its configuration holds the VPS address of hop 1.
steps.defender: the mail gateway may log the attachment. The install itself is silent.

steps.title: The first hop - the only one you see
steps.caption: The implant beacons out. The firewall forwards the connection to the VPS on port 443. This is the last hop before your network boundary, and the only relay your logs can identify.
steps.defender: one new TLS destination on a rented cloud ASN. Volume is low and steady.

steps.title: Hidden hops and the ORB
steps.caption: The VPS forwards to the compromised router. The router hands the traffic into a Tor network, which reaches the hidden C2 service. These hops are dashed in the diagram because you cannot see them.
steps.defender: your egress logs show nothing new after the VPS.

steps.title: The ICMP variant
steps.caption: Between relay nodes the chain can use ICMP instead of TCP. The C2 commands ride inside ping-like packets. No TCP session appears.
steps.defender: a small rise in outbound ICMP volume on the WAN link, but no content is visible.

steps.title: SOC signal and correlation
steps.caption: Two alerts fire close together. First, the workstation beacons on a fixed schedule to a rented-ASN address. Second, EDR flags the implant process that owns the connection.
steps.defender: process plus pattern on the same host is high confidence. Open a case.

steps.title: Block, pivot, and hunt
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the VPS address at the firewall. The operator answers by rotating to a new hop 1 within hours. The team starts a hunt for the pattern, not just the IP.
steps.defender: block the first hop, then hunt for the next one by timing, process, and protocol.
